p1_b3.ocr: Key columns, such as the “Conversion Rate” and “Average Order Value (AOV),” provide insight into how effectively live commerce is translating viewer interest into actionable sales. In 2018, the live commerce sector witnessed the emergence of platforms that integrated social media with direct purchasing capabilities, creating a dynamic shopping experience. With a staggering audience of 150 million users engaging with live commerce events, the potential for conversion was substantial; however, the challenge lay in converting this interest into sales. The conversion rate, notably recorded at 5.0%, reflects the initial effectiveness of these platforms in engaging users and motivating them to complete purchases. This figure serves as a baseline for understanding the growth trajectory of live commerce as it has become more mainstream. Furthermore, the Average Order Value (AOV), recorded at £25.00, underscores the purchasing behaviour being exhibited by consumers in this evolving market.

p1_b4.ocr: As brands refine their strategies and enhance the interactive elements of their live commerce offerings, it is anticipated that both conversion rates and AOV will experience upward trends. The data outline not only the current state of live commerce but also the opportunities for improvement and innovation that lie ahead. With user engagement figures reaching 30 million active participants per event, brands have a unique opportunity to craft tailored experiences that drive higher conversion rates. By fostering a direct connection with consumers through live interactions, brands can significantly enhance customer loyalty and, ultimately, sales performance. The landscape of live commerce is continuously evolving, and the insights derived from these metrics will be instrumental in shaping future strategies. As we delve deeper into the subsequent sections of this report, we will explore the implications of these trends on market positioning and competitive advantage, providing a holistic view of the live commerce ecosystem in Europe.
